checks.subject: the verdict whether the issue may be refined

steps.reason: whether this process already wrote its comment on the issue is a machine check over the comments just read; a wrong verdict here would write the same sections twice

conditions.not_matches: Written by Taktus, process P-02 Refinement

checks.subject: the list of sections the issue lacks

steps.reason: which sections of the ready standard the issue lacks is the standard's own reading of its body — the rule `ready`, the same code a session's `make backlog` runs, rather than a `check` with patterns that would state the standard a second time and could drift from it; an issue that is closed or a pull request is refused here, and one that carries every section lacks none: the steps that write sections skip themselves, and the run finishes having written nothing

rejected.why: whether a section is there is a fact of the text, not a judgement

checks.subject: the sections written

fallback.when: the answer fails the check, or the model serving the purpose reasoning is unavailable

steps.reason: writing what must be achieved, how it is verified and where the boundary lies from an issue's text and its discussion is understanding language and judging what "done" means for it; no rule expresses that

no labelled corpus of such sections exists yet; a classifier cannot write them

work.pattern: ^### (What must be achieved|How it is verified|Where the boundary lies)[ \t]*\n+\s*\S
work.system: You write the missing sections of a task in a software backlog. You are given the names of the sections that are missing; write exactly those, each headed "### " and the name, in the order given, and no other section. "What must be achieved" states the outcome, not the route. "How it is verified" states the conditions that must hold, as a list of testable sentences, so that it cannot be met by interpretation. "Where the boundary lies" states what is not part of it. Cite the issue's own words where a sentence comes from them. Write nothing before the first heading.

checks.pattern: Once they are in the issue, a person adds the label `ready`; P-03 Implementation reads
checks.subject: the composed text

steps.reason: the comment is the model's sections plus a fixed footer that says who wrote them

rejected.why: a fixed composition needs no model

work.text:
${sections}

---
Written by Taktus, process P-02 Refinement, from the issue and its comments: the
sections of the ready standard the issue lacks (docs/process/README.md). Edit freely.
Once they are in the issue, a person adds the label `ready`; P-03 Implementation reads
the issue, not this comment.

steps.reason: writing a comment is an API call with a fixed body; the effect leaves the system

rejected.why: nothing here needs a sandbox or tools

takeover.sequence: It runs whenever an issue is opened in the repository. By hand, the owner, or a person the owner named, starts it when a new issue appears, for that one issue. The seven steps run in order: read the issue, read its comments, stop if the sections were written before, find the sections of the ready standard the issue lacks, write exactly those, put them into one comment, and post it. If nothing is missing, the person stops and writes nothing. The issue itself is never edited and the label ready is never added.

admit.do: look for a comment that contains "Written by Taktus, process P-02 Refinement"; if one is there, stop: the sections were written before, and nothing is written twice
admit.done: no such comment exists, or the process stopped here

compose-comment.do: put the sections into one comment and end it with the fixed footer: a line, then "Written by Taktus, process P-02 Refinement, from the issue and its comments", saying that a person adds the label ready once the sections are in the issue. Keep that footer sentence, so that a later run finds the comment and writes nothing again
compose-comment.done: the comment holds the sections and the footer

missing.do: note which of the three sections of the ready standard are missing or empty: "What must be achieved", "How it is verified", "Where the boundary lies". If the issue is closed or a pull request, stop. If none is missing, stop and write nothing
missing.done: the list of missing sections is noted, or the process stopped here
missing.expertise: the ready standard of the backlog, in the repository's process document under Ready

credentials.where: the operator's secret store, under the parameter REPOSITORY_TOKEN described in CREDENTIALS.md; a person may instead use their own account, if it may read issues

read-comments.do: read every comment on the same issue, in order
read-comments.done: every comment on the issue is read

credentials.where: the operator's secret store, under the parameter REPOSITORY_TOKEN described in CREDENTIALS.md; a person may instead use their own account on the repository hosting service, if it may read issues

read-issue.do: open the issue whose number the run was started with and read its title, its body and its state; note whether it is a pull request
read-issue.done: the issue's title, body and state are read
read-issue.expertise: finding an issue by its number

refine.do: write exactly the missing sections, in the order of the standard, each headed with three hash signs, a space and its name, and no other section. What must be achieved states the outcome, not the route. How it is verified states testable conditions as a list. Where the boundary lies states what is not part of it. Use the issue's own words and its discussion; invent no requirement
refine.done: each missing section is written, opens with its heading and has text under it
refine.expertise: understanding the issue's subject well enough to say what done means for it, and writing conditions a test can check

credentials.where: the operator's secret store, under the parameter REPOSITORY_TOKEN described in CREDENTIALS.md; a person may instead use their own account, if it may comment

write-sections.do: post the comment on the issue; do not edit the issue and do not add the label ready
write-sections.done: the comment is on the issue, and the issue and its labels are unchanged
